chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, who said:

I asked Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him), so I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! We were companions with a people in Mecca, so we departed from them, and we carried some of their goods without knowledge. The people had gone, and we do not know them, nor do we know their homelands. So the goods remained with us, so what shall we do with them?'
He said: 'You carry it until you catch up with them in Al-Kufa.'
Yunus said: 'I said to him, 'I do not know them, and we do not know how to ask about them.''
He said: 'Sell it and give its price to your companions.'
So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! The people of Wilayah?'

key_terms.الْوَلَايَةُ: Wilayah (guardianship/authority, referring to the Imams or their deputies)
key_terms.عَبْدٌ صَالِحٌ: Abd al-Salih (a title often used for Imam al-Sadiq in this narration)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on goods left behind by people who departed without notice?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the practical application of *khums* and the authority of the Imams in managing unclaimed property (*al-mal al-mafqud*). It highlights the jurisprudential nuance where, if the original owners are unknown or untraceable, the proceeds from selling their goods are allocated to the 'Ahl al-Wilayah,' affirming the Imams' role as custodians of community wealth in the absence of clear heirs.
